accepts.because: a fresh turn from the surface
the expectation set of a tool round

the brief of the turn's counterpart coming home (GH #834): affinity's answer to the `brief` this hive raised at the turn's opening -- or its error, stamped `hop.brief_outcome == 'error'`, which parks the leg empty -- restamped onto this lane by the member's edge and carried down by a v-lane. It is the third leg of a turn beside the window and the memory, and the fan-in waits for it whenever `assemble.brief_slots` is set. `context.counterpart` (an entity reference the entry edge of a channel with many counterparts stamps) is what the brief was about; it is optional and it is not a requirement of any lane here: a turn without it asks nothing and parks the leg empty

a delegation the voice model made of its own accord (welle-live, R-25-4): in a duplex call the model speaks to the caller itself and hands the backend an errand while it keeps talking -- tools, memory, the reasoning core. It is the SECOND event lane and is assembled exactly like `in_advice`: it belongs to a turn on the MODEL's clock, so it can re-enter no round of ours and opens a fresh one with the whole iteration budget. `context.delegation_id` is the correlation and rides in the row's `consult_id`, the seat an advice's consult sits in, because it is the same thing -- the half of a bilateral exchange the model can pass back. The row's role is `delegation`: it reads like a sentence of the caller's and is none, the errand is the model's own, quoted out of what it heard. On the wire it wears a frame that says all of it -- what it is, which id the answer travels under, what was last heard -- because the wire role stays `user`, the one inbound role every provider accepts mid-conversation
a round that ran out of iterations

the declarations coming back (GH #464): `schemas[]`, one `{name, description, parameters}` per name the tools hive has, and `unknown[]`, the declared names it has nothing under. This cell wraps each declaration in the provider envelope -- the hive answers provider-neutral on purpose, because a hive that wrapped would have to be told which provider its caller talks to -- and writes the result out on `menu`. An unknown name is REPORTED, in `hop.menu_unknown` and as a warn line in `log.jsonl`, never dropped: a name nobody has is a declaration in the agent's own template pointing at nothing, and seeing that is the whole value of declaring. **Retracted in 3.4.0 ([#529](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/529))**: up to 3.3.1 this lane wrote the result straight out on `menu` and the one answer it carried WAS the menu. That is withdrawn. One reply is the whole menu only while exactly one thing answers, and the moment two do the second would not merge with the first, it would DELETE it -- the write is a `$replace` -- so the two answerers would take the menu away from each other on every tick forever. A second answerer is required, because a tool the composite reaches by an edge on its NAME is topology of the level that draws the edge and only the side that ANSWERS a call can declare it. So this lane now RECORDS the answer as one row of the hive's own `menu` table (columns `answerer`, `tools`, `unknown`, `recorded_at`), keyed by `context.tool_answerer` -- the mirror of the `tool_caller` a request already carries; absent, it is the one-answerer shape and counts as the default answerer, so a tree wired before this behaves exactly as it did -- reads every row back in the same bundle (delete + insert + select, the GH #419 form, phase `menu-merge`), and the answer to THAT bundle derives the menu as the union over all the rows and emits it on `menu`. The empty-menu guard stands in front of the write and now covers the row as well: an answer with no usable declaration records nothing and leaves this answerer's stored row untouched. And the unknown names travel INTO the row rather than being reported here, because a name this answerer has nothing under may be one another answerer delivers: the finding is computed against the MERGED menu and the warn line moved to the merge with it

the graph moved, so ask the tools hive again (GH #553). It is the DOOR the menu tick used to have no need of: `./menu-clock` sat inside this hive and stamped the internal lane itself, and a five-minute poll is what an event-driven substrate pays for a question that already has an answer. The door below turns it into `in_menu_tick`, which stays internal -- a caller names this lane, never that one

emits.because: the seam: one round, whole, for the curator that owns the window (R-27-1, GH #889) -- the caller's edge carries the iteration bound and restore_ttl
a memory read this turn needs

the brief this turn asks for (GH #834): one `tool_call` in affinity's request shape (`{subject, channel, slots}`) under an id derived from the turn and the subject, `hop.turn_id` the turn it belongs to. Raised once at the turn's opening, beside `recall`, only with `assemble.brief_slots` set and a `context.counterpart` to be briefed about. Who asks and in which round are edge truth: the member's edge that turns it into `in_brief` stamps the asker, and the turn's `audience_set` rides along

the turn is finished. Since collector@3.5.0 a round that spent its ITERATION budget is told apart by hop.partial == '1' and ends on a NAMED PARTIAL ANSWER -- one assistant text turn saying which bound it hit, what it called and the head of the last result -- instead of on the raw end of the tool round, which is what a consumer that reads the last text used to hand a person (GH #570). hop.round_capped is stamped there. Since collector@2.1.1 a THIRD sort travels here and it is told apart by `hop.degraded`, not by `round_capped` (which such a message does not carry): a turn that could not be assembled at all because the store refused a read or a write (GH #343). `hop.store_error` carries the store's `error_code`, `hop.store_operation` the op it refused, and the text names both. A parent that renders an answer must branch on `degraded` -- without it a failure reads as a real reply

the names this agent declares it uses, on their way to the tools hive's `in_schemas` door (GH #464). The whole body is `{"tools": [...]}` and `["*"]` asks for everything: the hive keeps no table of who asked, so the request says what it wants every time. A parent that wires the tick MUST wire this and the answer back, or the tick fires into a dead letter every period

the answered menu, as `system.tools` and nothing else (GH #464). It is durable state and not a projection of one round: the curator keeps the subtree per slot path (`in_slots`) until something overwrites that exact path, and no turn travels beside it. The subtree carries `$replace`. **Retracted in 3.4.0 ([#529](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/529))**: up to 3.3.1 this said the menu becomes exactly what the hive answered, and that is withdrawn. One answer is the whole menu only while exactly one thing answers; with two, the second would delete the first instead of merging with it. What travels here is the UNION over every answerer's last submenu -- kept one row per `context.tool_answerer` in the hive's own `menu` table and walked in answerer order, so the same rows always derive the same menu and the first answerer wins a name collision. `hop.menu_answerers` names the answerers the menu was derived from, beside `menu_count`, `menu_self` and `menu_unknown`. Both empty-menu guards stand: an answer with no usable declaration writes nothing AND records nothing, and a merge that came out empty writes nothing either, rather than an empty menu that would revoke the model's whole tool set. A store that refuses the merge is a warn line and a STOP, never a `degraded` answer: a menu is durable state with no turn beside it, so there is nothing to report into, and the next tick asks again. Wire it into the curator's `in_slots`

description.purpose: Scope marker of the collector hive: bundles the assembly state machine and its state surface. THE HIVE IS THE ADDRESS — everything from outside is sent to the hive itself, never to a cell inside it, and the hive hands it on. What an agent's LLM needs of a round is gathered in here, in one place, instead of spread over a persona cell, a prep cell and a tool-loop collector; what enters its window is the curator's (R-27-1, GH #889).
description.use_when: One per agent brain. Instantiate per agent tree and wire the parent's edges TO THE HIVE PATH (`./collector`), not to anything below it — see meclaw-overview § Die Hive-Grenze. `params.ports` is empty and therefore sealed: a mutation that reaches inside is rejected with hive_port_boundary.
description.not_in_scope: No inference, no persona, no tool fan-out, no durable memory. And no knowledge of its inside for anyone outside: which cell answers a lane is this hive's business and may change without touching a caller. And NO SCHEDULE AT ALL since GH #553: `./menu-clock` fired one question whose answer overwrites one slot, which was harmless -- and it was still a poll, so the mutation receipt took its place. The stale-round exit is the schedule this hive always refused: it would decide when somebody's round falls.
description.contract_in: Every message whose `hop.route` starts with `in_`, plus the one that does not. The ELEVEN lanes in use: in_turn (a fresh turn), in_advice (an advisor's answer), in_delegation (a delegation the voice model made), in_bundle (a memory bundle), in_briefing (the brief of the turn's counterpart, GH #834), in_calls (the expectation set of a tool round), in_tool (one tool result -- every turn of its `messages[]`, never just the first, and never its `system` slot: GH #252), in_answer (the brain's answer), in_round_sweep, in_menu (the tool declarations coming back from a tools hive, GH #464), and mutation_committed (the mutation door's receipt, carried in by the level above, GH #553 -- the one lane here whose name does not start with `in_`, because it keeps the name it was given at the door). Eleven doors, twelve lanes the state machine dispatches on: the twelfth, in_menu_tick, is INTERNAL, and it is this hive's own door from mutation_committed into ./assemble that names it -- a lane nothing outside can send is not a door; a lane declared here that nothing behind the door reads would be a door into silence, which is why in_batch left in 2.0.1 and in_close, in_prune, in_thread_call and in_pack left with GH #889.
description.contract_out: Everything the assembler emits that is not an in_ lane and not the internal cstore write, leaving through the hive path: curate (the seam -- one round, whole, for the curator; the caller's edge carries the iteration bound and restore_ttl, GH #889), recall, brief (GH #834), answer (THREE sorts: a real answer, a capped round told apart by hop.round_capped -- and, since 3.5.0, by hop.partial, which comes with a partial answer as the last turn instead of the raw round end, GH #570 -- and -- since collector@2.1.1 -- a turn the store would not let be assembled, told apart by hop.degraded, which carries no round_capped; a reply edge must guard on BOTH keys, GH #343), schemas (the declared tool names, for the tools hive's in_schemas door) and menu (the tool menu as durable system.tools, for the curator's in_slots; since 3.4.0 it carries the UNION over every answerer's stored submenu rather than one answer, with hop.menu_answerers naming the answerers it was derived from, GH #529). A caller wires the ones it needs and ignores the rest. write, turn_write, prune, pack and pack_ack left with GH #889: episodes, the close batch and the pack are the curator's.
